c135.title: A Wedding in India
c135.story: Anna's college friend Priya invited her to a wedding in India. All the women wore bright [[saris|sari]], and Anna wore a borrowed one too. Priya's grandfather wore a white [[dhoti]], and her uncle wore a red [[turban]]. The uncle is a [[Sikh]], and he loves telling old stories. He told Anna about a [[raja]] who ruled a small kingdom near a river. His neighbor was a [[maharaja]], a much greater king with a far bigger palace. In the story, a foreign visitor made the servants call him [[sahib]]. After lunch, a snake charmer showed the guests a [[cobra]] in a basket. In the evening, the family went to the temple for a [[puja]]. An old [[mystic]] read prayers in [[Sanskrit]] with his eyes closed. At the end, he gave everyone sweet [[prasad]]. Anna said it was the most beautiful day of her year.

c136.title: Istanbul, Dubai and Cairo
c136.story: Max's parents took a long trip around the Middle East this spring. In Istanbul, they went shopping in an old [[bazaar]] and bought a blue amulet for Max. In Dubai, they visited a palace where a [[sheikh]] once welcomed guests. The guide said that Dubai is the biggest city of its [[emirate]]. In a nearby country, the ruler has a different title: he is the [[emir]]. Then they rode camels across the desert to a green [[oasis]]. On the way, Max's dad saw a lake, but it was only a [[mirage]]. In the morning, a [[scorpion]] was sleeping in his shoe! In Cairo, they heard the morning prayers at an old mosque. They saw the Great [[Sphinx|sphinx]] and took a boat trip on the Nile. Back home, Max's dad laughed and said he now checks his shoes every morning.

c141.title: Dad's Small Bakery
c141.story: Last year, Anna's dad decided to become a [[businessman]]. Anna's mom, a [[businesswoman]] with her own flower shop, gave him lots of advice. He opened a small bakery with his old friend Taras, who became his [[business partner]]. First, they wrote a [[business plan]], and Anna helped them check the [[cash flow]] every week. After six months, the bakery made its first small [[profit]]. They kept their [[pricing]] simple: every pie cost the same. They chose a local [[vendor]] for flour and bought a delivery van from a [[dealer]]. Soon a big [[retailer]] wanted to sell their bread in its stores. Taras had worked in [[retail]] before, so he knew what to say. They hired a [[sales manager]] named Iryna and joined a farmers' [[cooperative]] for fresh milk. Sometimes they even used [[barter]] and paid the farmers with fresh bread. Now a regional [[distributor]] takes their pies to five towns.

c142.title: Max's Startup
c142.story: Max and two friends started their own [[startup]] last spring. As the [[founder]], Max had to explain the idea to everyone. The [[concept]] was simple: an app that plans cheap, healthy meals for students. Their [[business model]] was a small monthly payment. Max showed a simple [[use case]]: a tired student opens the app and finds dinner. An [[investor]] named Mrs. Bondar listened carefully. She said the app could be a [[game changer]] for busy students. She offered them a [[win-win]] deal and asked to join their [[venture]]. She put in the [[capital]], and the team brought their [[know-how]]. Soon they got a [[patent]] for their smart shopping list. A newspaper called Max a young [[innovator]], and his mom put it on the fridge. Now a food delivery company wants to start a [[joint venture]] with them in Poland.

c143.title: Anna's Marketing Seminar
c143.story: Anna is studying [[marketing]], and on Friday she went to a [[seminar]] at her university. The teacher gave the class a [[case study]] about a small juice company with weak [[branding]]. A real [[art director]] helped Anna's team create a new [[logo]] and a [[slogan]]. Then they talked about [[targeting]] and decided to sell the juice to the [[mass market]]. Most [[respondents|respondent]] in a survey liked the green bottles. They compared their sales numbers with a [[benchmark]] from a bigger company. Anna suggested a summer [[promotion]]: buy two bottles, get one free. They also designed a simple [[landing page]] and planned some [[email marketing]] for old customers. Next week, Anna has a hands-on [[workshop]] where students make real ads together. In May, professors from many countries will give long talks at a big [[symposium]]. The teacher liked Anna's project so much that she can present it there!
